chapter: Minton's, Louis Armstrong and the South
title: Closeness with Louis; the pot in the middle of the night
summary: Armstrong adopted him; he could wake Louis at any hour, and was sent by other band members to ask for his marijuana.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And he reached back in the book and said, 'I'll get Little Gizzard. Play this.' And when we pulled out the music and I went right through it, and he said, 'Doggone, Gizzard.' And that was my man. He was my man from then on. I could wake Louis up any hour of the night when nobody would dare. I would knock on the door. And Percy Woods was singing with us at the time. Remember Percy Woods, the tenor?

They would say, 'Kenny, are you crazy, man? Don't do that.' I said --like we wanted to get high, you know, and I knew Pops had some pot. So they wanted to get high, but they put me up to do it. Then they would say, 'Watch yourself.' And they would be on the steps, preparing to run, you know? So Pops comes out of the door, you know. So I would knock, and he would say, 'Who is it?' And I'd say, 'Gizzard.' He'd say, 'Oh, is that you, Gizzard?' Open the door, put two sticks of pot in my hand. And then Ann Baker and them would stand on the steps and say, 'Come on.' You know. And I would have to go turn them on. But I could wake Pops up any hour of the night. That's how close we became. Isn't that something?
And what did it feel like to be drumming back of that sound and everything?
